articles.body: It's 2019. There is no AI. You get a ticket: "Center the signup modal. It must work in IE11." You have a search engine, a Q&A site called StackUnderflow, and copy-paste. Every search, every tab, and every build costs in-game minutes. Your coworkers ping you. Your lead calls a standup. How long does your shift take? That's beforeai.dev, a small browser game I shipped this week. It's free, needs no signup, and takes about 5 minutes to play. 🎮 How it plays Search: Tappable query chips (or type directly on desktop). Open answers: Some are closed as duplicate. Some are from 2011. One suggests a jQuery plugin. Copy, then "Paste + build": Builds take ~4 minutes.

articles.title: Cache consistency when the data changes rarely
articles.excerpt: Fee schedules are the ideal shape of data for a cache: small, read constantly, and almost never change. That last property is also what makes them dangerous. A cache that is right for eleven months an…
articles.body: Fee schedules are the ideal shape of data for a cache: small, read constantly, and almost never change. That last property is also what makes them dangerous. A cache that is right for eleven months and silently wrong for three days does not look like a bug — it looks like the exchange changed its rates and nobody updated the site. Here is the cache design I ended up with, and the three failure modes that pushed me there. Failure 1: a TTL is a bet on someone else's release schedule The obvious cache is a TTL. Pick 24 hours, store the schedule, refresh once a day. The problem is that the TTL has to be wrong in one of two directions: Too short , and you hammer an endpoint that returns the same bytes 364 days a year, paying latency and rate limit for nothing.

articles.title: Your Website Looks Great. So Why Isn't It Working?
articles.excerpt: The Problem Nobody Notices Until the Website Goes Live Imagine spending weeks perfecting a website. The typography is beautiful. The animations are smooth. The colors are carefully selected. The homep…
articles.body: The Problem Nobody Notices Until the Website Goes Live Imagine spending weeks perfecting a website. The typography is beautiful. The animations are smooth. The colors are carefully selected. The homepage looks like something straight out of a premium design gallery. Everyone loves it. Then the website goes live. People visit. They scroll. They leave. The contact form barely gets used. Mobile visitors disappear. Search engines struggle to understand certain pages. And suddenly, someone asks the uncomfortable question: "Why isn't our beautiful website doing anything?" Here's the problem: a website can look exceptional and still fail at its actual job.

articles.title: Dharma-AI releases 2B Field Extractor for document-to-JSON
articles.excerpt: Dharma-AI published details of Field Extractor on Hugging Face on November 4, 2026. It is a 2-billion-parameter model for pulling specific fields out of documents. Plain OCR returns all the text on a…
articles.body: Dharma-AI published details of Field Extractor on Hugging Face on November 4, 2026. It is a 2-billion-parameter model for pulling specific fields out of documents. Plain OCR returns all the text on a page and leaves someone to write code that maps each string to a database field. This model returns structured JSON instead. Two ways to ask The model accepts a document image plus one of two request types: Open: no schema is supplied. The model works out from layout and context which parts are fields, such as a label followed by a value or a table with a header row, and returns key-value pairs. Schema-directed: you specify the fields you need, assigning each a type (string, number, or boolean), using the key names already in place in your system.

articles.body: Disclosure: I am from the aiFetchly team. This article is written for small business owners and operators, not as a sales pitch — the routine below works with any local document library, and I mention aiFetchly only briefly at the end. The problem is not writing speed Most slow customer replies are not caused by slow typing. They are caused by scattered sources: a price list in one PDF, a warranty note in another, a delivery policy buried in an email thread, and a product detail remembered by one person on the team. When the answer is not in one place, every reply becomes a small research project. The result is often generic wording, a guess, or a long delay while someone checks.

articles.excerpt: Modern applications need more than basic image uploads. A single photograph may require a square version for Instagram, a wide crop for a website banner, an optimized copy for mobile devices, and a wa…
articles.body: Modern applications need more than basic image uploads. A single photograph may require a square version for Instagram, a wide crop for a website banner, an optimized copy for mobile devices, and a watermark for ownership. Creating and storing every variation manually wastes time and storage. That is why I built Cloudinary Photo Gallery & Image Editor (CPGIE) , a browser-based image management and transformation studio powered by Cloudinary. The Problem Developers and content creators regularly face several media-management challenges: Large images slow down websites. Standard cropping can remove faces or important details. Different social platforms require different dimensions. Permanent watermarks modify the original image.

articles.title: Your SPF and DKIM passed last month. Here is why they can fail today without you touching DNS
articles.excerpt: A one-time email authentication setup is a snapshot. The records you published can stay byte-for-byte identical while the result changes, because several parts of the check live outside your zone. inc…
articles.body: A one-time email authentication setup is a snapshot. The records you published can stay byte-for-byte identical while the result changes, because several parts of the check live outside your zone. 1. SPF includes are nested, and you do not control them include: pulls in another domain's record, which can include more domains. SPF allows at most 10 DNS-querying mechanisms per evaluation (RFC 7208, section 4.6.4). If a provider you include adds an include of its own, your total can cross 10 with no edit on your side. The receiver then returns permerror and SPF fails. Count yours recursively.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force launched an experimental Super Strypi rail-launched rocket carrying 13 tiny satellites, but it failed just after liftoff from Hawaii.
articles.body: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms.

articles.body: When "Star Trek" celebrated its 60th anniversary in September, it was a strangely muted affair. Sure, there were fan events, screenings, and even an attempt at a world record for the biggest simultaneous Vulcan salute in history , but the lack of a "Doctor Who"-style birthday episode felt like a glaring omission. It was like everyone had shown up for the party, but the organizers had forgotten to book the headline entertainment. Luckily, there were rather more fireworks for the show's 30th birthday, when both "Voyager" and "Deep Space Nine" marked the occasion in style. "Voyager" episode "Flashback" took Tuvok (Tim Russ) back to his days on the USS Excelsior bridge alongside Original Series vets Hikaru Sulu (George Takei) and Janice Rand (Grace Lee Whitney).

articles.title: NASA's Swift space telescope crashes back to Earth after failed rescue attempt
articles.excerpt: NASA's Swift space telescope crashed back to Earth today (Nov. 4), three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost the observatory to a higher orbit.
articles.body: NASA's Swift space telescope has reached the end of its long and winding road. Swift fell uncontrolled to Earth today (Nov. 4), 22 years after it launched but just three months after a private spacecraft was supposed to boost it to a higher, life-extending orbit. The 3,200-pound (1,450 kilograms) observatory reentered Earth's atmosphere at 7:39 a.m. EST (1239 GMT) today over northern Sumatra, according to satellite tracker Jonathan McDowell , who cited U.S. Space Force data. The fall likely didn't make much of an impact; NASA officials predicted beforehand that most of the minibus-sized Swift would burn up as it fell, and they put the odds of any of the surviving pieces hurting anyone on Earth at just 1 in 2,100.

articles.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
articles.excerpt: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead" but new spacecraft observations suggests the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping.
articles.body: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead," but new spacecraft observations suggest the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping. That means that Olympus Mons , the extinct Martian volcano that at around 16 miles (26 kilometers) above the surrounding Martian plains is the largest mountain in the solar system , may in fact be a slumbering giant. The observations were made with the European Space Agency (ESA) mission ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) as it studied volcanic fissures along the Alba Mons region of the Red Planet. Alba Mons is in the Tharsis region of Mars, the same area that is home to Olympus Mons.
